clue.text: Landing-site boss is going round perimeter

indicators.note: the word for boss is placed around the other piece, enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: a boss is the head of an organisation
a lip is the edge or rim of something, its perimeter

explanation.surface: A manager walks around the edge of an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a person in charge, but here it means the head; 'going round' wraps it around the word for an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter touches down on a small marked pad, its own landing-site.

clue.text: Chopper engineer starts to examine turbine

parts.note: to engineer a scheme is to hatch it, to devise it in secret

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken, the starts of each

explanation.surface: A mechanic begins inspecting a helicopter's turbine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' and 'turbine' suggest a helicopter, but the definition means a small axe; 'engineer' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe for cutting wood is a tool that chops, so it is a chopper.

clue.text: Very quick to take to an audience?

definitions.text: Very quick to take to an audience?

parts.words: Very quick to take to an audience?
parts.note: an idiom for very fast, read literally as something that would suit a crowd who applaud, since clappers are applauders

explanation.surface: Someone asks what would be the fastest act to put before a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for 'very fast' is read literally: an audience is full of people clapping, so the phrase fits them.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means at great speed, the clappers being the striking parts of a bell rung hard.

clue.text: Very well-groomed, with superior cut

indicators.note: the word for superior is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: prime means of the best quality, superior

explanation.surface: Someone is immaculately turned out, with a haircut of the highest class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a haircut, but it signals that PRIME loses its last letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prim is stiffly neat and proper in appearance, as tidy as can be.

clue.text: Opening for the men in party system

indicators.note: the men are placed in the middle of the words for party and system, split between them

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a way is a method or system of doing things
OR, other ranks, means the ordinary soldiers, the men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A political opening is offered for male members within the party machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party system' sounds like politics; 'in' places the men, OR (other ranks, soldiers below officers), between the words for party and system.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is an entrance or gap in a wall through which one passes, an opening.

clue.text: Spoil nearly everything in a marriage

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or damage it

indicators.note: the phrase for everything is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: it all, as in 'that's it all', means everything

explanation.surface: Someone warns against ruining almost everything within a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everything' is the phrase 'it all', and 'nearly' drops its final letter; 'in a marriage' is an adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to wedlock, describing what happens within a husband-and-wife union.

clue.text: Tune has mother hiding unexpected smile

indicators.note: the word for mother surrounds the other piece, concealing it inside

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: the letters of smile come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A mother conceals a surprising smile while humming a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tune' is the definition: a melisma is a musical term for a decorative run of notes on one syllable. 'hiding' has the word for mother wrap the reshuffled smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A melisma is a run of several notes sung to one syllable, a melodic passage in a song.

clue.text: Nothing to be found in computer memory range

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is located inside the computer word, placed within it

parts.note: RAM is random-access memory, the working memory of a computer
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: No trace turns up anywhere in the computer's memory range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' ends the clue as part of 'memory range', but it is the definition, a verb meaning to wander.
explanation.definitionFit: To range is to wander freely over an area, the same as to rove about.

clue.text: Drunk's threat to clothing?

explanation.surface: A tipsy person's clumsiness puts their clothes at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the idiom literally: wear, as in clothing, getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is drunk is in a bad state, the idiom meaning damaged or the worse off; literally, clothes worn out by use.

clue.text: A chance event left China powerless

indicators.note: the word for china loses its P, the symbol for power

parts.note: china is fine pottery, porcelain ware

explanation.surface: By chance, the left-wing government left China without electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is crockery, POTTERY; 'powerless' removes P, the physics symbol for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw of tickets where winning depends on luck, an event decided by chance.

clue.text: Indifferent attitude towards computers etc?

parts.note: the idiom for not caring either way, read literally with IT meaning information technology, computing

explanation.surface: Someone describes a lukewarm feeling towards technology.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is information technology, so a phrase saying one can accept or ignore it describes a casual view of computers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses that one does not mind whether an offer is accepted or refused, an indifferent stance.

clue.text: Dislike hurry, wasting sec-ends

indicators.note: the word for hurry wastes away, losing the letter for second

parts.note: haste means hurry or speed
sec is short for second, abbreviated further to S

explanation.surface: Someone hates rushing, as it squanders their precious seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sec-ends' as printed is a scan misreading of 'seconds'; either way the second is abbreviated S, the letter that 'wasting' removes from the word for hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate something is to dislike it intensely; a strong synonym for the verb.

clue.text: High-class stockist's first desire

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word for stockist is taken, its first

parts.note: a wish is a desire or longing

explanation.surface: An upmarket shop's main ambition is to stock luxury goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-class' leads the clue as a description of the stockist, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for smart and fashionable, describing something posh or upmarket.

clue.text: Undertake exercises to get drug info

parts.note: to do a task is to undertake it
PE, physical education, means exercises done at school

explanation.surface: Someone works out to learn about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope is slang both for a drug and for inside information, so either half of 'drug info' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for an illegal narcotic and also for the inside story or information on something.

clue.text: Child, one locked in grainstore

indicators.note: the letter for one is shut inside the building for grain, enclosed by it

parts.note: a barn is a farm building used to store grain
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A youngster is trapped inside a granary.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is a Scottish and northern English word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is a Scots word for a young son or daughter, a little one.

clue.text: Cut tail of blue bird

parts.note: to snip is to cut with scissors

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, so only the end of blue is used

explanation.surface: Someone trims the tail feathers of a bluebird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue bird' reads as one creature, but 'blue' only supplies its last letter and 'bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The snipe is a wading bird with a long straight bill, found in marshes.

clue.text: Those people accepting a charge for treatment

indicators.note: the words for those people take in the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: they means those people
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

explanation.surface: A group agree to pay a fee for medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a fee, but here it is RAP, an American slang word for a criminal accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is a course of care meant to heal or relieve an illness or condition.

clue.text: Many set for release in this?

definitions.text: Many set for release in this?

indicators.note: the letters of many set are released, freed to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether many prisoners are due to be freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for release' rearranges MANY SET, and the whole clue describes the answer, a general pardon when many are freed.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon, often freeing a large number of prisoners at once.

clue.text: Star, not quite elderly, resident in European city

indicators.note: the shortened word for elderly lives inside the city name, placed within it

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France, a European city

indicators.note: the word for elderly is incomplete, missing its last letter

parts.note: old means elderly

explanation.surface: An ageing celebrity lives in a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity, but it is the definition: a real star. 'not quite' cuts the word for elderly to OL, and 'resident in' houses it in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the Pole Star, the bright star nearly above the north celestial pole.

clue.text: Where to get more fuel? Coal-mine's best

parts.note: a pit is a coal-mine, and the 's adds an S
top means best, as in top quality

explanation.surface: Someone praises a colliery as the finest source of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuel' and 'Coal-mine' suggest coal, but the definition is a motor-racing refuelling stop.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, a car pulls off the track for petrol and new tyres during a race at this stop.

clue.text: Subdues member of new family

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a new relative firmly in line.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is 'steps on', to crush or subdue.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps on means treads down, quells; a stepson is a spouse's son from an earlier marriage, joining a blended household.

clue.text: Redesigned University with help of prospective worker

indicators.note: the letters are redesigned, put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A job applicant helped redesign a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redesigned' rearranges U with HELP and OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful is a candidate hoping for a job or success, an aspiring applicant.

clue.text: Year one's brought in to cut a heap of grass

indicators.note: the pieces for year and one are brought inside the word for cut

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly
I is the Roman numeral for one; the 's means 'has' and supplies nothing

explanation.surface: Once a year someone mows a field and piles up the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in to' places the abbreviation for year and the numeral for one inside the word for cut; the 's of 'one's' is a link meaning has.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayrick is a large stack of dried mown grass, kept as fodder.

clue.text: Criminal leader getting round Yard on various levels

indicators.note: the scrambled leader surrounds the letter for yard, getting round it
a criminal version of the word is a crooked, rearranged one

explanation.surface: A gang boss evades Scotland Yard at every level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' evokes Scotland Yard, but it is the unit, Y; 'Criminal' rearranges LEADER into LAERED, which 'getting round' wraps around Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something layered is built up in tiers or strata, at several heights.

clue.text: Time to copy a cassette

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: Now is the moment to duplicate a tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copy a cassette' suggests duplicating, but 'copy' is APE, mimicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette holds magnetic recording strip on spools, the medium for sound recording.

clue.text: Upset most of Yankee country

indicators.note: the letters are upset, knocked over into a new order
only most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone distresses nearly all of an American's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final E of YANKEE, and 'Upset' rearranges YANKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is an East African nation on the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Small creatures surrounding one in battle

indicators.note: the word for small creatures goes round the letter for one, enclosing it

parts.note: fry are young fish, small creatures
a means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: Tiny animals encircle a lone fighter in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small creatures' are FRY, young fish, not insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a fight or skirmish, as in 'enter the fray'.

clue.text: Make for the capital of Majorca

indicators.note: the capital letter, the initial, of Majorca is taken rather than its chief city

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for Palma, the chief city of Majorca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the capital of Majorca' wants to be Palma; it means the initial letter, M.
explanation.definitionFit: To form something is to shape or create it, to make it.

clue.text: Observe first of cases in hospital

indicators.note: the opening letter of cases is placed inside the word for hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Doctors watch the first patients arriving at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital for long-term patients.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over or examine something closely, to observe it.

clue.text: No-one's watching this art coalesce, possibly

indicators.note: the letters might possibly be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist hopes their work blends together while unobserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THIS ART COALESCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means it is safe to proceed because nobody is looking or in the way.

clue.text: Job on island for delivery agent

parts.note: a post is a job or position
Man is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job on an island delivering things.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A postman brings letters and parcels to homes, a courier of mail.

clue.text: Affectionate, glowing family

parts.note: kind means warm-hearted and affectionate
red means glowing, as embers glow red

explanation.surface: A warm, radiant household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family' is the definition here, used as an adjective meaning related.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's relatives, those related by blood.
